country.comment: Single-district case study of the Sabar Shouchagar Project in Nadia district, West Bengal, India, with national background context on India.
country.where_found: PDF p. 2, Title and Introduction (p. 1); PDF pp. 2-4, Background and The Nadia story (pp. 1-3)

effect_estimate.comment: Descriptive before-and-after program and third-party validation figures only; no regression or inferential statistical estimates (no CIs or p-values) are reported. Exhibits 1-6 (PDF pp. 13-16) are embedded image figures without extracted text.
effect_estimate.value: Descriptive case study — no inferential effect estimate reported. Following district-led multi-agency coordination (pooling MGNREGA, NRLM, NBA, Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, and ICDS resources across 6,620 catchment areas), alignment of Gram Panchayats and district political leadership, expansion of women-SHG-run rural sanitary marts from 9 to 107 plus 2 permanent mason training centres, mandatory household open-defecation-free declarations, and village Neighborhood Monitoring Committees (Para Najardari Committees), 0.35 million sanitation facilities were built over 20 months/2 years (covering over 3,36,000 families, 4,240 schools, all 6,620 ICDS centres, and rail/road encroachment habitations), increasing district sanitation coverage from 60% to 97% and toilet usage from 57% to 99.8% (UNICEF validation of ages 4+ in April 2015, declaring Nadia India's first open-defecation-free district).

mechanism_certainty.comment: Rated 2 (capped at 2 by qualitative/descriptive case-study design ceiling): the paper directly documents how multi-agency administrative resource pooling, hierarchical catchment-area governance, administrative persuasion/fund leverage over Gram Panchayats, SHG sanitary-mart capacity building, household ODF declarations, and neighborhood compliance monitoring operated to achieve sanitation coverage and toilet adoption, corroborated by cited UNICEF/HIJLI Inspiration validation findings on panchayat institutional pressure, although presented in a pedagogical case format without a formal primary methods section.

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines territorial division into 6,620 ICDS catchment areas of 200-250 households (planning, service_area), inclusion of rail and road encroachment habitations usually overlooked in government sanitation schemes (accommodation), multi-department coalition building overcoming agency silos across MGNREGA, NRLM, NBA, SSA, and ICDS (institutional_fragmentation), alignment and persuasion of elected Zilla Sabadhipati and Gram Panchayat representatives alongside district bureaucrats (political_coordination), state/SHG supply-chain facilitation via 107 rural sanitary marts and 2 mason training centres (bureaucratic_assistance), mass community/SHG/school mobilization (participation), and mandatory household ODF declarations plus village Para Najardari Committees monitoring violators and real-time web tracking (ENFORCEMENT).
